messages:
Olivia (PM): kicking off a short PRD intake for a small but important ask — per-route safety contracts + automatic failover behavior for hosted API customers.
Ben G: +1. can you paste the problem statement/goals as you have them?
Olivia (PM): problem: customers want predictable, tenant-scoped safety constraints (max tokens, model family whitelist, response latency ceilings) and a deterministic fallback when their primary model violates policy or capacity. goal: define required fields, success metrics, and launch acceptance criteria for a minimal MVP. non-goal: building a full policy engine or per-tenant model training.
Jia Li: quick Q: when you say "deterministic fallback" — do you mean an automatic switch to a pinned variant or an immediate reject response?
Olivia (PM): preference is automatic switch to a compatible variant (lower-cost/quantized or smaller family) + mirrored audit log entry. only reject if no compatible variant exists or explicit tenant setting is reject-only.
Sara W: acceptance criteria suggestion: 1) tenant policy schema defined + validated at create time, 2) runtime enforces max_tokens and model whitelist 3) fallback decision executed within 50ms of detection 4) audit log contains pre/post decision details.
Priya N: success metrics to track: % of requests that used fallback, mean added latency from fallback, false-positive rate (fallback when primary would have been fine), and number of tenants that configure safety-contracts in 1st 30 days.
Mike K: infra concerns: need to surface model compatibility map (which families are compatible fallbacks). Also we should avoid blocking hot path with external DB lookups. propose caching policy objects in memstore with TTL.
Ben G: edge cases: streamed responses mid-flight — how do we switch? graceful approach: allow current token stream to finish then route new request to fallback, unless tenant opted for immediate cutover. note this affects perceived latency/consistency.
Jia Li: for rollout: feature flag gated; start with non-prod tenants + 5 pilot customers, then open opt-in. Can we define canary success thresholds?
Olivia (PM): proposed canary thresholds: fallback success >= 99% (no crashes), avg end-to-end P95 latency increase <= 30ms, no increase in customer-visible errors > 0.1% relative.
Sara W: spec item: schema (example):
```
{
  "max_tokens": 2048,
  "model_whitelist": ["redwood-1", "gemini-small"],
  "fallback_policy": "auto-switch", // options: auto-switch | reject
  "immediate_cutover": false
}
```
Ben G: please add an explicit field for "allowed_quantizations" — some customers need to forbid int8.
Olivia (PM): noted. owners: Olivia (product) + Ben (runtime) + Jia (serving infra). ask: engs — can you comment by EOD on feasibility and any hard blockers? i'll collate into PRD draft tomorrow.
eng-bot: Reminder set for 2134654290 to review PRD draft. :bell:
Priya N: also need a short checklist for compliance: KMS boundaries for audit logs, retention policy, and whether fallback triggers are included in SOC reports.
Mike K: one more: how do we test fallback quality? propose synthetic workload that forces capacity limits and policy triggers, plus a small set of real-customer prompts (sanitized) for regression checks.
Olivia (PM): perfect — i'll assemble into a one-pager with the schema, acceptance criteria, canary thresholds, and test plan. thanks all :rocket:
